profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google[x]
profile.summary: Developing innovative solutions for autonomous unmanned systems, robotics, and real-time embedded systems.  Strong passion for the integration of software, hardware, and algorithms; software development; inertial navigation; control systems; and real-time embedded systems.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Oct 2017: Now focusing on self driving cars at Waymo.
Aug 2014 -- Oct 2017: Enjoyed working on an amazing green energy project (Makani).

positions.title: Navigation Engineer IV
positions.description: Sought to increase performance and bring software development best practices to an inertial navigation system for sub/super-sonic air vehicles.

positions.title: Principal Engineer II
positions.description:
Sought to bring indoor pedestrian navigation to first responder markets.  Redesigned the algorithm to meet customer deployment requirements, real-time embedded computation requirements, and to significantly increase the overall navigation performance, consistency, and robustness.

Firefighter Location
- Inspired change; proposed and encouraged an alternate DSP-based design to address SWaP-C concerns that ultimately led to a successful product; wrote all supporting software.
- Designed, developed, and analyzed the inertial navigation algorithm.
- Developed innovative techniques to address customer deployment use cases.
- Developed all real-time embedded software, including boot loader, drivers, and application.
- Implemented real-time embedded software on a TI TMS320C6745 DSP and PIC18.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: Teamed with a diverse group of engineers to solve the indoor pedestrian navigation problem.  Developed innovative software solutions that led to improved inertial navigation performance, including the derivation of new virtual measurement corrections, detection of virtual measurement opportunities, and detection/handling of elevators and escalators.

positions.title: Engineer
positions.description:
Developed an expertise in real-time embedded systems and inertial navigation for autonomous unmanned systems using embedded Linux.  Developed passion for autonomous unmanned land and underwater vehicles.  Collaborated with vendors and sensor manufactures to improve software integration and navigation performance.

Remote data recovery project (classified)
 - Developed navigation algorithms an autonomous underwater vehicle.

Underwater vehicle simulation
- Developed an underwater vehicle simulation to accelerate development and reduce risk.
- Developed kinematic framework to relate rigid bodies in a generic fashion.
- Developed accelerated ray-tracing algorithms to simulate multi-beam and side-scan sonar, Doppler, and acoustic ranging sensors.
- Engaged with industry vendors to facilitate and enhance utility of simulation.

Autonomous underwater vehicle for ship hull inspection
- Led technical development effort, responsible for original proposal.
- Reverse engineered an unsuccessful vehicle to create a development platform of opportunity.
- Developed vehicle navigation, mission planning, guidance control, topside communications, sensor integration, and vehicle infrastructure algorithms.
- Achieved outstanding results at AUVFest '07.

Swimmer interdiction system
- Developed embedded software solutions an autonomous distributed buoy system.
- Implemented algorithms to communicate with and reward marine mammals.

positions.title: College of Engineering, Control Systems Lab Graduate Assistant
positions.description:
Developed an expertise in real-time embedded systems and control systems for computer control of mechanical systems and robotics using DSPs and micro-controllers.  Developed passion for the integration of software, hardware, and control theory; robotics; DSPs and micro-controllers; and sensors.

Graduate Assistant classes and roles
- Computer Control of Mechanical Systems.
- Mechatronics.
- Modeling and Analysis of Dynamic Systems.
- Developed embedded software and hardware to incorporate new technologies into lab exercises.

Thesis development work
- Created the mechanical and electrical design for a complex 10-link, 12-revolute joint parallel mechanism with an unstable pendulum attached via an universal joint on the end-effector.
- Developed the kinematic and dynamic models (equations of motion).
- Developed the feedback linearization control to stabilize the pendulum (inverted) in free space.
- Implemented real-time algorithms on a TI TMS320C6713 DSP.

publications.title: Underwater Inertial Navigation With Long Baseline Transceivers: A Near-Real-Time Approach
publications.publisher: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology · May 25, 2015
